en: Itivuttaka 68: Tikanipāta, Dutiyavagga Thus it was said. In the third group of threes, the second chapter. “Monks, there are these three kinds of persons found existing in the world. What three? The person who is like a stone, the person who is like a water jar, and the person who is like a lotus. And how, monks, is one a person like a stone? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. When he dwells thus, he gives rise to thoughts of harm; having given rise to thoughts of harm, he acts upon them. This is called a person like a stone. And how, monks, is one a person like a water jar? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. When he dwells thus, he gives rise to thoughts of harm; having given rise to thoughts of harm, he does not act upon them. This is called a person like a water jar. And how, monks, is one a person like a lotus? Here, monks, a certain person dwells with a mind full of hate, harboring ill will toward beings. When he dwells thus, he gives rise to thoughts of harm; having given rise to thoughts of harm, he neither acts upon them nor relishes them. This is called a person like a lotus. These, monks, are the three kinds of persons found existing in the world.”
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
“Bhikkhus, for whoever lust has not been abandoned, hatred has not been abandoned, and delusion has not been abandoned—”
“Monks, this one is called ‘bound by Māra, with Māra’s snare fastened around his neck, subject to the doing of the Evil One as he wishes.
But whoever, monks, has abandoned lust, abandoned hatred, and abandoned delusion— this one, monks,
is called ‘unbound by Māra, with Māra’s snare cast off, not subject to the doing of the Evil One as he wishes.’”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
With reference to this, it is said:
And ignorance has been faded away;
him, the one with developed self,
the Tathāgata who has become Brahmā— him I honor.
“The Buddha, who has transcended enmity and fear, is said to have abandoned everything.
This meaning too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
